CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING

CALL  TO ORDER  Gil Hurtado,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to order  at
  6:55 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve  Costley,  Director  of Parks  & Recreation

PLEDGE  OFALLEGIANCE  Betsy  Camano,  Recreation  Coordinator

PRESENT  Mayor  Gil  Hurtado,  Vice  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Council  Member  Maria  del

  Rios;  City  Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager  Rob  Houston,  City
  Attorney  Rail  F. Salinas

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  - NON-AGENDA

ITEMS  Erik  Denials,  40-year  resident  lives  on the Eastside  of the 710 freeway  and
  has an issue  with  a light  pole.  We all have been  in the dark  for 3 months
  and have  seen a rise in crime.

  Lizette  Ruiz,  Resident  lives  on Kauffman  is requesting  assistance  in
  cleaning  up the railroad  tracks  on Independence.

  Issues  at Hollydale  Park  in the play  areas and is requesting  an upgrade.
  Children  play  with  sand,  and it is dirty.

  Ruben  Pichardo,  Resident  is reporting  iSSues regarding  emails  sent to
  council  and go unanswered.  The  issue with  Johanna  has not stopped.  She
  continues  to go to his home  and takes  pictures.  Code  Enforcement  tells
  him  there  is no problem  with  his trailer.  Mr.  Pichardo  need transparency
  and a resolution  to his issue.

  Jane Denial,  Resident  lives  on Garfield  and Imperial.  She witnessed  a
  transient  with  a cardboard  home,  and it was recently  removed.  Thank  you.
  What  can be done  with  the homeless  issue on Imperial?

  Ana,  Director  of the Chamber  of Commerce  provides  information
  regarding  the Thanksgiving  Dinner  event  and Christmas  Parade.

EMAILS:  Mario  Dominguez  is requesting  the addition  of a camera  for Media  Dept.
  employee  Giselle  Hernandez.  Also,  is asking  when  construction  will
  resume  at the Urban  Orchard  location?

LAW  ENFORCEMENT  The City  Council  unanimously  approved  items A, B & C during  Consent
  Calendar:

  a.  Authorized  utilization  of the 2024-2025  Selective  Traffic  Enforcement
  Program  ("STEP")  Grant  Funds  in the amount  of $1 70,000  for
  overtime,  equipment,  and training  expenses;

  b.  Amended  the Fiscal  Year 2024/25  Law  Enforcement  Grants  Fund
  Budget  by appropriating  $123,402  for overtime  salaries,  $43,341  for
  equipment,  and $3,257  for training  expenses;  and

  c.  Authorized  the Chief  of Police  to execute  the STEP Grant Agreement
  (Contract  No. 2024-98-CC)  in a form  acceptable  to the City Attorney.

6

LAW  ENFORCEMENT  The City  Council  unanimously  approved  items A, B, C & D during
  Consent  Calendar:

  a.  Authorized  utilization  of 2022 Homeland  Security  Grant  Program
  Funds  in the amount  of $45,577  for law enforcement  equipment  to
  address  civil  unrest,  crowd  control  and active  shooters;  and

  b.  Increased  the Fiscal  Year 2024/25  revenue  projection  in Account
  Number  232-541  (Law  Enforcement  Grants  - Homeland  Security
  Grant)  to $45,577;  and

  c.  Amended  the Fiscal  Year 2024/25  Law Enforcement  Grants  Fund
  Budget  by appropriating  $45,577  to Account  Number  232-541-21-
  6204 (Law  Enforcement  Grants-Homeland  Security  Grant - Small
  Tools  and Equipment);  and

  d.  Authorized  the City  Manager  to execute  the State Homeland  Security
  Grant  Program  Subrecipient  Agreement  (Contract  No. 2024-99-CC)
  for Grant  Year 2022.
